title: The Night of the Long Watch

collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE III: DEFENSE, RAIDS AND THE FALLEN (LCC-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
"If anyone comes to raid our homeland, we'll be ready." Isola's people are peaceful but no pushovers: stamping dances and war chants, watch fires and plans, raids fended off or not, prisoners and bargains, and how the village honors those who defended it.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: Raiders' fires burn on a nearby islet all night: watch until dawn, or send someone to see.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: Fires have been burning all night on the little islet off the north beach: raiders, camped, waiting. (subject), (friend) and (third) are on watch. (third) wants to swim over and count them. (subject) says nobody leaves the beach. (friend) is just trying to stay awake. What should they do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: They watch all night, taking turns to sleep. At dawn, the fires on the islet go out, and the raiders' canoes leave in the other direction. The village never learns what they wanted. (third) still wishes (third.he/she) had gone to see.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (third) swims over silently and comes back an hour later, shivering, with a count: twelve raiders, two canoes, and a great deal of arguing. The village has its warriors on the beach by dawn. The raiders see them and leave.
